_comment: Arm B for the `cd` posture question. The shipped text PROHIBITS cd; this arm states the FACT the prohibition is standing in for -- that the working directory does not carry over between calls. Hypothesis: a model re-anchors with `cd` because it is trained against a bash tool whose cwd DOES persist, so under that prior the cd is correct defensive behaviour and a bare prohibition argues with a belief it never addresses. Measured on a dogfooded session, anthropic models opened 1,095 of 1,114 bash calls with `cd` (98.3%) against the older wording, while a codex model in the same session, same text, used it 0 of 62 times. Everything except the third paragraph is byte-identical to the shipped text -- arm-diff.py must report exactly one differing row.
tool.bash.description:
Run a shell command with %s. The tool merges stdout and stderr.

Use the dedicated tools instead of the equivalent shell commands. Use read, write, and edit for files, and do not use cat, sed -i, or echo. Use grep and glob to search, and do not use the grep, find, or ls commands. The dedicated tools are safer, easier to review, and cheaper.

Every command starts in %s. The working directory does not carry over from one command to the next, so a `cd` at the start of a command changes nothing and a `cd` at the end is forgotten. A relative path applies to that directory. It does not apply to the directory of the file that you read or changed last. For a path outside that directory, give an absolute path or use `git -C`.

Do not force-push and do not run `reset --hard`. Do not amend a commit, bypass hooks, or run `git add -A`. Do these git operations only if the user asks for them. Do not print or send out secrets such as .env files, tokens, or credentials.

For a slow command, set the timeout. The default timeout is 120 seconds, and then the tool stops the command. In a script with many steps, do not use `set -e`. One failed step stops the full script and hides the other results. Examine the exit code of each step instead. The tool puts $TERVA_HOME in the environment.
